policy: Independent semantic review of this exact document corpus; executable replay verifies identity and cited evidence, not general semantic analysis, runtime behavior, registration or deployment conformance. Unreviewed clauses remain NOT_RUN.

rows.text: When defining values for use with publicKeyMultibase and secretKeyMultibase, specification authors MAY define additional header values for other key types in other specifications and MUST NOT define alternate encodings for key types already defined by this specification.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: The condition is authoring publicKeyMultibase or secretKeyMultibase header values. The reviewed SAGE corpus defines neither; chapter 10 explicitly excludes emitting Multikey and specifies JWK projection instead. NOT_APPLICABLE is limited to this absent header-definition activity. It does not approve a new header, another key encoding, third-party extensions or runtime key handling.

rows.text: Representations MAY define other extensibility mechanisms, including ones that do not require the use of the Decentralized Identifier Extensions repository.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: The permission concerns a representation author choosing another extensibility mechanism. SAGE defines record-to-document projections using the named standard representations, not a new representation or representation-level extensibility mechanism. Resolution metadata under sage and A2A AgentExtension are separate objects, not such mechanisms. The unexercised permission is NOT_APPLICABLE, not PASS for implementing or refusing extensions.

rows.text: Such extension mechanisms SHOULD support lossless conversion into any other conformant representation.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: Such extension mechanisms refers to the additional representation-level mechanisms in extensibility.2. None is defined by this SAGE author corpus. The conditional author recommendation is NOT_APPLICABLE for that reason only. The two record projections deliberately differ in verification-method type and are not lossless reserializations; no arbitrary representation-conversion or standard implementation conformity is certified.

rows.text: Extension mechanisms for a representation SHOULD define a mapping of all properties and representation syntax into the DID document data model and its type system.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: This recommendation addresses the author of a representation-level extension mechanism. SAGE defines none in this corpus. Its record projection table, resolution metadata and A2A extension do not define one. NOT_APPLICABLE does not establish a complete abstract-data-model mapping or certify third-party mechanisms.

rows.text: Syntaxes used to express the data model in this specification SHOULD be identified by a media type, and conventions outlined in this section SHOULD be followed when defining or using media types with DID documents.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: For the DID 1.1 projection reviewed under this DID 1.1 clause, DIDP-01 explicitly uses application/did, the exact standard context and JsonWebKey; DIDP-02 and RESOLVE-03 keep the requested document projection and contentType distinct from the application/json resolution envelope. This is a documentary judgment of the selected standard media identification and its document/envelope convention only. It does not certify legacy application/did+json registration or aliasing, all media-type conventions, actual HTTP negotiation, representation-author obligations or producer/consumer conformance.

rows.text: A DID method specification MUST define how authorization is performed to execute all operations, including any necessary cryptographic processes.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: Controller/operator scopes, expected versions, proof checks and atomic authorization decisions are defined. However, the authenticated meaning of the controller identifier and its binding to credentials for every management operation are delegated to selected bindings. Proof of possession explicitly does not authorize mutation. The reviewed corpus does not close that all-operations principal/credential mapping and its necessary cryptographic processes. This is a remaining semantic contract, not a generic W3C demand for an ABI or successful deployment.

pending_review.required_actor: method specification author with a complete selected profile/binding document
pending_review.reason: Controller/operator scopes, expected versions, proof checks and atomic authorization decisions are defined. However, the authenticated meaning of the controller identifier and its binding to credentials for every management operation are delegated to selected bindings. Proof of possession explicitly does not authorize mutation. The reviewed corpus does not close that all-operations principal/credential mapping and its necessary cryptographic processes. This is a remaining semantic contract, not a generic W3C demand for an ABI or successful deployment.
completion_evidence: Identify and freeze documentary evidence for the selected authorization binding, without assuming any particular API, ABI or transaction format.

Review authentication and credential-to-controller/operator binding for every operation, including the operation/registry/DID binding and required cryptographic processes; distinguish PoP from mutation authorization.
Close the all-operations semantic contract from documentary evidence; live execution remains a separate actor.

rows.text: A DID method specification MUST specify how a DID controller creates a DID and its associated DID document.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: The controller chooses the canonical identifier before constructing registry/DID/key-bound proofs. Chapter 09 sections 1, 3 and 4 define the bounded initial record, unused identifier reservation, proof validation, authenticated creation and atomic version-1 created state. The eip155 profile adds account-bound commitment/reveal and separate activation; the web profile defines the trusted origin and authenticated administration. Chapter 10 sections 1, 2 and 6 specify the associated document projection, including the empty verificationMethod array and omitted relationship members for created records. This discharges the abstract creation procedure on the same documentary criterion as deactivation; concrete deployment authorization and execution remain distinct scopes.

rows.text: A DID method specification MUST specify how a DID resolver uses a DID to resolve a DID document, including how the DID resolver can verify the authenticity of the response.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: Chapter 10 defines DID-to-registry selection, validation and projection; chapter 09 defines authenticated TLS-origin web reads and finalized eip155 observations. The remaining whole-method semantic contract is how the selected trusted source is authenticated and establishes its chain/network identity, readiness and response authenticity, including eip155. The web branch alone and a source-name metadata string do not discharge that whole-method duty. A specific ABI or successful live response is not an additional W3C author requirement.

pending_review.required_actor: method specification author with a complete selected profile/binding document
pending_review.reason: Chapter 10 defines DID-to-registry selection, validation and projection; chapter 09 defines authenticated TLS-origin web reads and finalized eip155 observations. The remaining whole-method semantic contract is how the selected trusted source is authenticated and establishes its chain/network identity, readiness and response authenticity, including eip155. The web branch alone and a source-name metadata string do not discharge that whole-method duty. A specific ABI or successful live response is not an additional W3C author requirement.
completion_evidence: Review the selected source/readiness and response-authentication documentary binding across the supported method profiles, including eip155.
Connect the exact DID/profile to authenticated source identity, chain/network binding, finality/readiness and failure handling; distinguish a configured source label from authenticated evidence.
Close this author obligation from sufficient documentary evidence without requiring a particular ABI or substituting a live response for the specification.

rows.text: A DID method specification MUST specify what constitutes an update to a DID document and how a DID controller can update a DID document or state that updates are not possible.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: Chapter 09 sections 1, 3 and 9 define updates: immutable key additions, retained revocations, replacement of services, lifecycle changes and scoped grant mutations with their exact public-record effects. The controller or an eligible scoped operator uses the current expected version; authorization, transition validation, history, grants and the next record commit atomically or nothing changes. Controller transfer, key-material replacement, identifier reassignment and operator redelegation are excluded. Chapter 10 sections 1, 2, 3 and 6 map the resulting record to its document and metadata. This discharges the abstract update procedure on the same documentary criterion as deactivation; it does not certify every operation's authenticated-principal binding or a deployed update.

rows.text: The DID method specification MUST specify how a DID controller can deactivate a DID or state that deactivation is not possible.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: Deactivation is a terminal transition from created or active, with a readable record; mutations require the authenticated controller or explicitly delegated operator and expected previous version. Concrete deployment authorization remains a distinct review scope. Chapter 09 section 9 defines scoped controller delegation and chapter 10 section 3 distinguishes readable inactive records from denied key use.

rows.text: A DID method specification MUST define exactly one method-specific DID scheme that is identified by exactly one method name as specified by the method-name rule in 3.1 DID Syntax.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: Exactly one current did:sage method name is declared by the case-sensitive did-sage production; registry kinds are formats within that method, not additional DID method names.

rows.text: A DID method specification MAY specify ABNF rules for DID paths that are more restrictive than the generic rules in Path.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: The closed DID-URL ABNF in chapter 06 includes no path production, and the surrounding normative text explicitly rejects paths. This records the permitted choice of a more restrictive DID path grammar only, not runtime rejection or application-specific dereferencing.

rows.text: A DID method specification MAY specify ABNF rules for DID queries that are more restrictive than the generic rules in this section.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: The closed DID-URL ABNF in chapter 06 includes no query production, and the surrounding normative text explicitly rejects queries. This records the permitted choice of a more restrictive DID query grammar only, not runtime rejection or support for standard optional DID parameters.

rows.text: A DID method specification MAY specify ABNF rules for DID fragments that are more restrictive than the generic rules in this section.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: The DID URL production restricts the fragment to key-id, with an explicit one-to-32 character ABNF. The MAY permits this selected restriction and does not require arbitrary fragment support.

rows.text: The DID method specification MUST specify how to generate the method-specific-id component of a DID.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: The client chooses an unused identifier before proofs; creation reserves it atomically. Chapter 06 defines its composition and chapter 09 sections 6 and 8 define the selected formats. Random generation is not a universal requirement of this clause.

rows.text: The DID method specification MUST define sensitivity and normalization of the value of the method-specific-id.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: Equality after the specified normalization defines sensitivity: kind and chain address are lowercase, percent encoding and non-normal forms are rejected, and remaining identifier characters compare as strings without an extra normalization.

rows.text: The method-specific-id value MUST be unique within a DID method.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: This MUST constrains actual method-specific-id uniqueness, rather than merely requiring a sentence in the method document. Registry uniqueness and non-reassignment declarations do not independently prove the generated identifiers are unique.

pending_review.required_actor: issuer of generated DIDs under the selected registry profile
pending_review.reason: This MUST constrains actual method-specific-id uniqueness, rather than merely requiring a sentence in the method document. Registry uniqueness and non-reassignment declarations do not independently prove the generated identifiers are unique.
completion_evidence: Establish the applicable registry identity, identifier allocation and non-reassignment assumptions.
Provide an independent uniqueness argument and appropriately attributed enforcement evidence for the generated identifiers.
Do not turn a declared guarantee or a few distinct fixture strings into global uniqueness evidence.

rows.text: Any DID generated by a DID method MUST be globally unique.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: This MUST constrains globally unique generated DIDs. The intended registry-plus-local-ID construction depends on registry identity and DNS/chain/fork assumptions; the document declaration and sample strings alone do not establish the property.

pending_review.required_actor: issuer of generated DIDs under the selected registry profile
pending_review.reason: This MUST constrains globally unique generated DIDs. The intended registry-plus-local-ID construction depends on registry identity and DNS/chain/fork assumptions; the document declaration and sample strings alone do not establish the property.
completion_evidence: Identify and justify the registry namespace and selected network/fork/DNS assumptions.
Connect the construction and local uniqueness/non-reassignment guarantees to independently attributed issuer evidence.
Keep unspecified operational trust and fork bindings unresolved, rather than choosing a deployment or treating a fixture as authority.

rows.text: A DID method MAY define multiple method-specific-id formats.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: The same method selects multiple method-specific-id formats: eip155 and optional web. Solana is explicitly reserved and cannot establish support. This judges only the documentary format choice.

rows.text: The method-specific-id format MAY include colons.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: The method-specific-id contains the registry kind, locator and agent-id separated by colons, under the single sage method. This is an exercised documentary permission, not a requirement to accept every colon-containing string.

rows.text: The DID method specification's Privacy Considerations section MUST discuss any subsection of Section 5 of [RFC6973] that could apply in a method-specific manner.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: The reviewed corpus lacks a method-specific privacy discussion of applicable RFC 6973 section 5 threats. Persistent DIDs, public controller/key/service records, retained history/tombstones and resolver observations make at least surveillance, stored-data compromise, misattribution, correlation, identification, secondary use, disclosure and exclusion relevant (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6973.txt, sections 5.1.1-5.2.5). Secret-key handling, encryption and charter N-4 do not discuss those method-specific privacy consequences. This is a substantive documentary omission, not failure solely for a missing heading, reference name or legal-compliance statement, and not a runtime privacy-breach finding.

rows.text: A representation MUST define deterministic production and consumption rules for all data types specified in 4.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: This clause assigns deterministic rules for every abstract type to the representation specification. SAGE authors record projections into existing DID representations, not a new representation. The new-representation-author activity is absent, so this SAGE author case is NOT_APPLICABLE. Deterministic rules in the adopted W3C representation and actual producer/consumer adherence remain separately assessable; the narrower SAGE projection table is not treated as a complete type mapping.

rows.text: A representation MUST be uniquely associated with an IANA-registered Media Type.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: The association obligation belongs to a representation definition. This corpus defines SAGE projections and media selection, not a new representation or new media registration. This SAGE new-representation-author case is NOT_APPLICABLE. It does not verify registration by naming a type, approve application/did+json as an IANA registration or alias, or transfer any media-registry question into PASS. The adopted representation and concrete media usage require their own evidence.

rows.text: A representation MUST define fragment processing rules for its Media Type that are conformant with the fragment processing rules defined in Fragment.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: The representation definition must supply generic media-type fragment rules. SAGE does not define a new representation; its canonical key URL and exact-ID method restriction are not replacement media-type fragment rules. This SAGE new-representation-author activity is NOT_APPLICABLE. The adopted W3C rules and actual generic fragment processing remain independently assessable.

rows.text: A representation SHOULD use the lexical representation of data model data types.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: This is a representation-author lexical-mapping recommendation. SAGE selects standard representations and constrains its record projections without defining a new abstract-type serialization. This new-representation-author activity is NOT_APPLICABLE. JWK coordinate encodings, protocol JCS and selected record fields do not prove a complete lexical mapping or actual serializer conformity.

rows.text: A representation MAY choose to serialize the data model data types using a different lexical serializations as long as the consumption process back into the data model is lossless.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: SAGE chooses no alternate representation-level lexical serialization. The conditional permission and its lossless-consumption condition are NOT_APPLICABLE to this absent author activity. This is not PASS for lossless conversion, input refusal or optional feature implementation; the adopted standard representation remains separately assessable.

rows.text: A representation MAY define representation-specific entries that are stored in a representation-specific entries map for use during the production and consumption process.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: SAGE defines no new representation-specific entries beyond the existing standard context choice; DIDP-01 fixes the standard DID 1.1 context string. This optional new-representation-author activity is NOT_APPLICABLE, not PASS for an abstract entries-map lifecycle. Actual producer/consumer handling and the adopted W3C representation-author rules remain separate cases.

rows.text: A DID method specifications MUST follow all guidelines and normative language provided in RFC3552: Writing Security Considerations Sections for the DID operations defined in the DID method specification.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: The reviewed method corpus does not describe the method-specific residual DoS susceptibilities and why avoiding them is unreasonable or out of scope, including repeated fresh authoritative reads and registry/DLT peer work. Charter N-1 and finite input/crypto bounds are useful but do not supply that analysis. RFC 3552 section 4.6 and section 5 require the susceptibility and exclusion reasons (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3552.txt). This established omitted requirement falsifies the composite documentary obligation; it is not failure merely because the RFC is not named, or a promotion of the separate SHOULD in security-requirements.13. Other incomplete authentication evidence is not converted into an additional proven failure.

rows.text: If a protocol incorporates cryptographic protection mechanisms, the DID method specification MUST clearly indicate which portions of the data are protected and by what protections, and it SHOULD give an indication of the sorts of attacks to which the cryptographic protection is susceptible.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: The PoP challenge, account-scoped commitment, web TLS and messaging protected fields are described. The complete protected/unprotected data boundary across the remaining management credential/source contracts is unresolved, consistently with method-operations.1/.3. This mixed MUST/SHOULD clause is not failed merely for an absent attack-susceptibility matrix or because a recommendation has not been proven.

pending_review.required_actor: method specification author with complete operation protection and source bindings
pending_review.reason: The PoP challenge, account-scoped commitment, web TLS and messaging protected fields are described. The complete protected/unprotected data boundary across the remaining management credential/source contracts is unresolved, consistently with method-operations.1/.3. This mixed MUST/SHOULD clause is not failed merely for an absent attack-susceptibility matrix or because a recommendation has not been proven.
completion_evidence: Map protected and unprotected portions of each required method operation to its actual selected cryptographic or authenticated-channel binding.
Specify principal/source association, termination/trust boundaries and the remaining susceptibility discussion; distinguish public record projections from signed PoP.
Resolve the actual binding semantics before a whole-method judgment, without inventing an operational authority or demanding successful deployment.

rows.text: Data which is to be held secret (keying material, random seeds, and so on) SHOULD be clearly labeled.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: CRYPTO-05 explicitly identifies fresh CSPRNG-generated secrets, ephemeral/private keys, shared secrets and expired traffic keys as material confined to the trusted boundary and excluded from logs. Registry public key bytes and public PoP/endorsement signatures are distinct from these secrets. This satisfies the documentary secret-labeling recommendation; it does not attest key custody, erasure, runtime logging or label every public nonce as secret.

rows.text: DID method specifications SHOULD explain and specify the implementation of signatures on DID documents, if applicable.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: The recommendation applies if the method uses signatures on DID documents. SAGE returns unsigned record projections and does not define a signature over the complete DID document. Registration PoP/endorsement, signed Cards/messages and authenticated source reads are different objects. The absent document-signature activity is NOT_APPLICABLE for this author case; this does not approve signature validity, unsigned-source authenticity or future document-signature schemes.

rows.text: Where DID methods use peer-to-peer computing resources, such as with all known DLTs, the expected burdens of those resources SHOULD be discussed in relation to denial of service.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: The eip155 profile uses DLT peer resources and requires eventual deployment cost/latency measurements. It does not discuss expected peer computation, storage/history retention or read/transaction burdens in relation to DoS, or justify omitting that discussion. Per-record bounds and a future measurement obligation are not that relation. This is a recommendation-level documentary FAIL, not a required runtime defect, an unperformed benchmark failure or a demand for specific measured fees.

rows.text: DID methods that introduce new authentication service types, as described in 5.4 Services, SHOULD consider the security requirements of the supported authentication protocol.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: This condition concerns a new authentication service type under DID services. SAGE defines discovery endpoints and the A2AInterface service vocabulary, whose authenticated application traffic does not introduce a DID authentication-service type. Services confer no authorization, and authentication remains in the named key relationships/protocol bindings. The absent new authentication-service-type activity is NOT_APPLICABLE; this does not exempt A2A, TLS or application-protocol security requirements.

rows.text: The Security Considerations section MUST document the following forms of attack for the DID operations defined in the DID method specification: eavesdropping, replay, message insertion, deletion, modification, denial of service, amplification, and man-in-the-middle.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: The charter and registry/resolution sections address modification, replay, withheld state and limited availability, but do not document method-operation amplification exposure or explain why that attack is inapplicable. Generic message replay protection, maximum sizes and cheap-check ordering are not a discussion of amplification for DID creation/update/read/deactivation. The all-listed-attacks documentary MUST therefore fails for this fixed corpus; no live amplification behavior or exploit is asserted.

rows.text: Other known forms of attack SHOULD also be documented.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: The charter and method security discussions identify additional concrete risks: identifier/key substitution and front-running, stale or selectively withheld state, rollback, malicious trusted sources, key compromise, SSRF and authority confusion. Chapters 06, 09 and 10 connect these risks to method-specific boundaries and mitigations. This satisfies the recommendation to document other known attacks in the reviewed method scope, not an exhaustive proof against every future attack or a runtime defense result.

rows.text: The Security Considerations section MUST discuss residual risks, such as the risks from compromise in a related protocol, incorrect implementation, or cipher after threat mitigation was deployed.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: The charter explicitly retains trusted capture/verifier/key and policy compromise, broken registry consensus or stolen controller credentials, metadata exposure and initially poisoned enrolment outside its claims. Registry and resolution security sections retain compromised protected signing boundaries and malicious trusted sources, while chapter 04 limits composition/forward-secrecy claims and requires further analysis. This is a documentary residual-risk discussion, not evidence that those assumptions hold, implementations are correct or a security proof is complete.

rows.text: The Security Considerations section MUST provide integrity protection and update authentication for all operations required by Section 7.2 Method Operations.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: Abstract lifecycle authorization, atomic version/history rules, PoP and source-observation requirements are present. The corpus still leaves the authenticated principal/credential-to-controller/operator association and whole-method authoritative-read authenticity contract to selected bindings. PoP alone is expressly not mutation authorization. Those known semantic prerequisites prevent closing integrity/update authentication for every operation; they are not a demand for a deployed ABI or a measured transaction.

pending_review.required_actor: method specification author with the selected administration and authoritative-read binding
pending_review.reason: Abstract lifecycle authorization, atomic version/history rules, PoP and source-observation requirements are present. The corpus still leaves the authenticated principal/credential-to-controller/operator association and whole-method authoritative-read authenticity contract to selected bindings. PoP alone is expressly not mutation authorization. Those known semantic prerequisites prevent closing integrity/update authentication for every operation; they are not a demand for a deployed ABI or a measured transaction.
completion_evidence: Review the complete selected principal/credential binding for create and every eligible mutation, including exact controller/operator/registry/DID/operation association.
Review integrity, replay/version and authenticated source-response handling across all required operations without treating PoP as authorization.
Keep this aligned with unresolved method-operations.1/.3; documentary closure needs complete semantics, not a successful live deployment.

rows.text: If authentication is involved, particularly user-host authentication, the security characteristics of the authentication method MUST be clearly documented.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: TLS-origin trust and abstract authenticated-controller/scoped-operator checks are stated. The security characteristics and assumptions of the management credential and its authenticated-principal mapping are not closed for all selected profiles. Saying authenticate the actor or use an authenticated transaction does not by itself specify that credential binding. No password, signer or trust root is chosen by this review.

pending_review.required_actor: method specification author with the selected controller/operator authentication binding
pending_review.reason: TLS-origin trust and abstract authenticated-controller/scoped-operator checks are stated. The security characteristics and assumptions of the management credential and its authenticated-principal mapping are not closed for all selected profiles. Saying authenticate the actor or use an authenticated transaction does not by itself specify that credential binding. No password, signer or trust root is chosen by this review.
completion_evidence: Identify the complete selected administration credential/principal binding and its authentication method.
Discuss its security assumptions, compromise/replay boundaries and association with the immutable controller or exact operator grant.
Close the author contract from documentary evidence without adding a particular API/ABI or deployment as a W3C requirement.

rows.text: The Security Considerations section MUST discuss the policy mechanism by which DIDs are proven to be uniquely assigned.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: Chapters 06 and 09 discuss the uniqueness policy: registry identity plus registry-local identifier, one canonical spelling, atomic reservation of unused identifiers, account-bound commit/reveal for eip155 and permanent non-reassignment/tombstones. They distinguish independently claimed human-chosen names and web-origin control. The clause requires discussion of the policy mechanism; it does not require this author case to prove actual global issuer uniqueness. Existing method-syntax.4/.5 remain unresolved, and no deployed enforcement or fork/DNS assumption is supplied here.

rows.text: Method-specific endpoint authentication MUST be discussed.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: Chapter 09 identifies the configured HTTPS origin/operator trust root, authenticated TLS, exact origin path, no redirects/downgrades, origin/destination allowlisting and no peer-chosen resolver. Its observation contract distinguishes self-validated nodes from explicitly trusted resolvers and requires source identity/network/readiness configuration; chapter 10 warns that TLS to an arbitrary resolver is not a blockchain proof. These are method-specific endpoint-authentication discussions, not completion of all source-authenticity bindings or an actual endpoint test.

rows.text: Where DID methods make use of DLTs with varying network topology, sometimes offered as light node or thin client implementations to reduce required computing resources, the security assumptions of the topology available to implementations of the DID method MUST be discussed.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: The reviewed eip155 method permits a self-validated node or an explicitly trusted resolver, not an unspecified light-client verification protocol. Chapters 09 and 10 discuss their different trust assumptions: configured source identity and chain/network/readiness policy, one finalized block, rollback rejection, restart readiness and the excluded malicious trusted registry/validator boundary. This judgment is limited to those documented modes. It does not certify consensus honesty/finality or extend to arbitrary thin/light-client topologies; no new topology is invented.

rows.text: The applicable DID method MAY specify how to dereference the DID path and/or DID query of the input DID URL.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: The method rejects DID paths and queries; this MAY does not mandate support.

rows.text: An extension specification MAY specify how to dereference the DID path of the input DID URL.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: No selected extension specification defining DID-path dereferencing was identified in this method snapshot.

rows.text: An extension specification MAY specify how to dereference the DID query of the input DID URL.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: No selected extension specification defining DID-query dereferencing was identified in this method snapshot.

rows.text: A conforming DID method specification MUST guarantee that each equivalentId value is logically equivalent to the id property value.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: equivalentId aliases are explicitly not emitted and do not affect authority. This author condition is separate from generic library acceptance of a literal metadata field.

rows.text: A conforming DID method specification MUST guarantee that the canonicalId value is logically equivalent to the id property value.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: canonicalId aliases are explicitly not emitted and do not affect authority. This author condition is separate from generic library acceptance of a literal metadata field.

rows.text: A specification that defines an error type not defined in this section MAY declare that it refines one of the error types defined in this section.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: SAGE-local errors and DID-interface mappings with sageCode are defined. A mapping between interfaces is not automatically a refines declaration in a custom DID error object.

rows.text: DID methods MAY allow multiple ways of implementing their "Resolve" operation, and SHOULD offer guidance regarding at least one way to implement a verifiable resolution.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: The method gives guidance for fresh verified records through self-validation or explicitly trusted authenticated resolvers; TLS alone is explicitly not blockchain proof.

rows.text: If a DID method uses such proofs, it MUST specify in its DID method specification how they are used for verification of the correctness of the result of a "Resolve" operation.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: The selected method relies on authenticated observations and key-registration PoP, not a specified portable proof of completeness/freshness of every Resolve result. If such proofs are selected, their verification specification is still needed.

rows.text: A DID method MAY also include such proofs in the DID document itself, or in a proof property of the DID document metadata.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: The selected DID document/metadata shape does not include a portable Resolve proof. Structural proof literals in library tests do not select such a method mechanism.

rows.text: Therefore, the specification of a DID method that uses a distributed system as a VDR SHOULD specify a means by which the VDR they are using can be disambiguated from such forks.
rows.scope: SAGE method/representation specification author only; never a runtime implementation verdict
rows.review_basis: Chain/network/source identity and finalized-block readiness are required. A fork with the same chain ID, address and code still needs an explicit disambiguation rule; do not assume those fields alone resolve the recommendation.
